title: How to Recover When You Miss an Internal Deadline
summary: Missed an IB internal deadline in DP2? Learn what to do in the first 24 hours, contact the right people, rebuild your plan, and submit safely.
body_markdown:
Missing an internal deadline in the **IB DP2 fall term** is serious, but it is not automatically irreversible. Contact the relevant teacher immediately, submit the most complete work you currently have, confirm the school policy, and propose a short, realistic completion plan.


September to November can be difficult because IAs, the Extended Essay, TOK, predicted-grade assessments, university applications, and new content often overlap. Your priority is to establish what was missed, protect your eligibility for assessment, and restore a workable schedule.


### Identify which deadline you missed


The term **internal deadline** can describe several stages. A missed planning checkpoint does not necessarily have the same consequences as a missed final submission date.


Deadline type What it usually means Immediate priority


Planning checkpoint A proposal, question, outline, method, or source list was due Send available planning evidence and request a revised checkpoint


Complete draft The teacher expected a version for permitted feedback Submit the current version and ask whether feedback remains available


Final school deadline Work was due for marking, authentication, or processing Contact the teacher and DP coordinator immediately


School upload stage The school is preparing work or marks for IB submission Follow the coordinator's instructions urgently


The IB does not publish one universal student-facing deadline for every school. For components such as the **Extended Essay** and **TOK** , IB submission requirements lead schools to establish earlier internal schedules. Your coordinator calendar and school policy therefore remain authoritative, even when an online IB date appears later.


Missing an early checkpoint may reduce the feedback available. Missing a final deadline can be more serious because the school needs time to authenticate work, mark components, standardize marks, and manage submission procedures.


### What to do in the first 24 hours


### Contact the appropriate teacher


Contact your subject teacher or supervisor as soon as you know the deadline has been missed, even if the work is incomplete. For a final IA, EE, or TOK deadline, also contact the **DP coordinator** when required by your school's procedure.


The coordinator can explain the administrative position but cannot necessarily override school policy. Do not wait for the work to become perfect before communicating.


### Preserve and submit existing work


Save the current document, export a PDF, and preserve version history, data, notes, drafts, and source records. These materials demonstrate progress and may help establish authenticity.


If the submission system remains open, upload the most complete honest version unless instructed otherwise. If it is closed, email the file and ask how it should be submitted. An imperfect draft gives the school more information than a blank submission.


### Send a solution-focused message


State what was missed, briefly explain any relevant circumstances, and offer a realistic next step. Avoid an emotional account or an impossible promise.


> Dear \[Teacher\],
>
>
> I missed the \[task\] deadline at \[date and time\]. I have attached my current version, which includes \[brief description\]. The remaining work is \[specific tasks\], and I can submit a checked version by \[realistic date and time\]. Please could you confirm whether this is permitted under school policy and whether any feedback remains available?
>
>
> Kind regards, \[Name\]


If illness, bereavement, technical failure, or another documented circumstance contributed, explain it accurately and ask what evidence is required. Never manufacture explanations, screenshots, or documents.


### Build a credible recovery plan


Base the plan on outputs, not intentions such as “work on the IA all weekend.” List each unfinished component and assign it to a time block.


Time block Concrete output


Day 1 Confirm requirements, secure files, submit current work, and complete the structure


Day 2 Finish analysis, calculations, evidence, or argument development


Day 3 Complete evaluation and conclusion, then check the criteria


Day 4 Verify citations, figures, formatting, word limits, and submission instructions


Prioritize **completeness before polish** . A complete argument containing evidence, analysis, evaluation, citations, and a conclusion is usually more useful than several polished pages followed by missing sections.


Use the assessment criteria and your teacher's instructions to identify the highest-value changes. RevisionDojo's guide to[what to do after missing an IA deadline](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/what-to-do-if-you-miss-an-internal-assessment-deadline) provides an IA checklist, while its[IA time-management guidance](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/time-management-strategies-for-completing-your-ia-on-schedule) explains how to create manageable milestones.


### Protect academic integrity under pressure


Deadline pressure does not relax academic integrity requirements. The IB's[academic integrity policy](https://www.ibo.org/globalassets/new-structure/programmes/shared-resources/pdfs/academic-integrity-policy-en.pdf) requires assessed work to be the student's own and expects schools to address integrity concerns before submission.


Do not ask another person or an AI tool to write assessed passages, conduct your analysis, invent data, or disguise copied material. Support may clarify concepts or criteria, but you must make the academic decisions and write the submitted work.


Record sources as you use them, distinguish quotations from paraphrases, and label data and images. Follow your school's referencing and AI acknowledgment rules.


### Protect the rest of the fall term


Do not abandon every other subject until the late task is repaired. This can resolve one emergency while creating several more.


During recovery, preserve a **20-30 minute** daily examination-maintenance block for retrieval practice or targeted questions. Give the overdue component the main work block. RevisionDojo's[balanced IB study schedule](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/how-to-create-a-balanced-ib-study-schedule) shows how coursework and subject revision can remain active together.


After submission, complete a deadline audit:


- Put every confirmed IA, EE, TOK, CAS, test, mock, and application date in one calendar.
- Label each date as a checkpoint, draft, final school deadline, or administrative stage.
- Set personal deadlines **3-7 days** before major school dates.
- Schedule weekly coursework blocks with named outputs.
- Review the calendar at the same time each weekend.
- Alert teachers early when a genuine obstacle develops.


The[DP2 month-by-month guide](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/month-by-month-guide-ib-dp2) places fall coursework within the wider year. The[full IB timetable guide](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/how-to-stay-organized-with-a-full-ib-timetable) explains how to maintain one reliable planning system.


### Common recovery mistakes


**Waiting for perfection:** Submit evidence of progress promptly. Once the deadline has passed, perfectionism can become avoidance.


**Using an online IB date:** Official pages for the[Extended Essay deadline](https://ibo.org/programmes/diploma-programme/curriculum/dp-core/extended-essay/submission-deadline/) and[TOK deadline](https://ibo.org/programmes/diploma-programme/curriculum/dp-core/theory-of-knowledge/upload-deadline/) explain why schools establish their own internal schedules.


**Demanding an extension:** Ask what is possible under the policy rather than assuming extra time is guaranteed.


**Promising an impossible turnaround:** Missing a second agreed date damages trust. Include checking and uploading time in your estimate.


**Rewriting everything:** Improve missing analysis, evaluation, evidence, and required components before adjusting minor wording.


**Hiding genuine circumstances:** Tell the appropriate staff member about health, accessibility, family, or technical problems and provide requested documentation.


### Conclusion


You can often recover after missing an internal deadline when you respond quickly and the school still has procedural room. Identify the deadline type, communicate immediately, preserve and submit existing work, follow school policy, and complete a criterion-focused plan without compromising academic integrity.


RevisionDojo can help rebuild your study system through Study Notes, Questionbank, Flashcards, Jojo AI, and coursework feedback tools. Your teacher and DP coordinator, however, remain the authorities on deadlines, permitted feedback, and submission decisions.
